column1: # Build targets: EESSI's supported CPU and GPU targets (eessi.io/docs,
# "Supported CPU targets" and "Supported GPU targets", page dated 2026-09-03,
# pasted by the operator 2026-10-24) against what ndexr builds and owns.
# ndexr_now   what the stack builds for it today. Every tree is
# native_on   an ndexr machine whose CPU (or GPU) IS this target, measured
#             2026-10-24 from the catalog's run records (itype) and lscpu:
#             intel = m7i, amd = m7a, arm = m7g, gpu = g5 (EPYC 7R32 + A10G),
# cuda rows   EESSI builds each capability for each CPU target (15 x 5 =
#             75 builds of one application in 2025.06); ndexr builds one binary
#             carrying several capabilities, for the generic CPU only.
# aws         an EC2 family with that CPU, where ndexr owns none. Not measured
#             here: check `lscpu` / archspec on the instance before a build.
